chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) and Muhammad ibn Abdillah narrated from Abdullah ibn Ja'far Al-Himyari, from Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar, from his brother Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Abi Al-Qasim, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Isḥaq ibn Ibrahim, from Harun, who said:

A man asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) while I was with him, saying: 'What is the reward for one who visits the grave of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him)?' He replied: 'Indeed, when Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was killed, the lands wept for him. So Allah appointed four thousand disheveled, dusty angels to weep for him until the Day of Judgment,' and he mentioned the rest of the hadith.
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting the grave of Imam Al-Husayn (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: This hadith from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat* underscores the cosmic scale of Imam al-Husayn’s martyrdom by describing how Allah appointed four thousand disheveled angels to weep for him until the Day of Judgment. In Shia tradition, this continuous celestial mourning serves as a spiritual validation of his sacrifice, linking the earthly tragedy to eternal divine recognition and emphasizing the profound connection between the Ahl al-Bayt and the created universe.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 12. My father and Muḥammad ibn ‘Abdillāh both narrated to me from ‘Abdillāh ibn Ja’far Al-Ḥimyari, from Ibrāhīm ibn Mahziyār, from his brother ‘Ali ibn Mahziyār, from Abil Qāsim, from Qāsim ibn Muḥammad, from Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm, from Hārūn (ibn Khārijah), who said:

One day while I was with Abī ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) a man asked him, “What is the reward for those who go to the Ziyārah of the grave of Ḥusain (a.s.)?” Imam (a.s.) replied – as part of a longer Ḥadīth – “When Ḥusain (a.s.) was killed, everything cried over him, even the (various) lands. Allāh has dedicated four thousand disheveled angels, who are covered with dust, to his grave and they cry over him (and will continue to do so) until the Day of Judgment.”
